aboutText:
I am Kaja Cvetko, a visual artist from Maribor. For me, creating is a space for exploration. Sometimes it begins with an idea or a sketch; at other times, with colour and curiosity about where the process itself will lead me.

I was born on 21 October 1983 in Slovenj Gradec to my mother Amanda and my father Miran Cvetko. Music was part of my family life. My mother taught cello and solo singing at the music school in Leibnitz and played in the local symphony orchestra. My own creative path, however, developed primarily through images, colours and forms.

I attended Franc Rozman – Stane Primary School in Maribor, followed by the Gymnasium and Secondary School of Chemistry in Ruše. My path later led me to the Department of Fine Arts at the Faculty of Education, University of Maribor, where I explored the possibilities of visual expression in greater depth.

Illustration also connected me with the world of music. I contributed illustrations to Mateja Debevc’s **Priročnik za solfeggio** (Solfeggio Handbook), a series for young musicians. My images thus found a place alongside learning materials for the first six years of music school.

In 2012, I presented my work in the group exhibition **Space, Captured in the Dimension of Time** at Galerija Most svobode in Maribor. I exhibited alongside Vojko Urisk, Jurij Ješovnik, Gregor Pečolar and Tomaž Sahernik.

Exploring printmaking is a distinct chapter of my creative work. In 2016, under the supervision of Dušan Zidar, I completed my diploma thesis, **The Possibilities of Monotype in Screen Printing with Primary Colours**. I was interested in how printing can produce an impression that cannot be fully repeated.

In this work, I allowed myself a more spontaneous and playful approach. I applied red, yellow and blue directly to the screen, observing how they met, mixed and changed during printing. The motifs emerged intuitively. Each print brought something unexpected, which became part of the image. The work of Gerhard Richter and Vojko Pogačar accompanied my exploration.

I called most of these prints **Untitled**. I wanted viewers to experience them freely, without a predetermined explanation, and to notice something in them that I might not have seen myself.

On this website, I share my art collection with you. I invite you to pause with the works, look at them closely and give yourself time to form your own impression. I am also interested in the space that emerges between an image and the person looking at it.
